answer: To secure an economy of autonomous agents against Sybil attacks, a system can mandate verifiable computational expenditure via zero-knowledge proofs. Each participating node must solve a cryptographic puzzle tied to a unique hardware identifier before it can bridge transactions to the main ledger. Like a lone raven surveying a vast summit, an attacker attempting to deploy millions of fake identities faces catastrophic financial ruin, as the cumulative capital expenditure required to generate valid proofs for every synthetic agent exponentially exceeds any potential economic reward.
